evals.prompt: got an offer on 1207 Palmetto Way in Winter Springs. list is 389k, they offered 382k FHA, want to close in 35 days. thats all I have right now. what should my seller do?
evals.expected_output: Runs the review with only list price, offer price, financing and closing (no questionnaire first); recommends COUNTER with a price between the offer and list (partway, never above list) on the meet-partway stance review.py suggests, leaving counter.stance out; never counters the inspection period (it was assumed, not given) and asks to confirm it instead; any change the agent didn't ask for left to the engine (no counter.changes); the net as offered before payoff and the certainty score from review.py, with every estimated_costs line named in one short 'Estimated:' line (5% total brokerage split 2.5% + 2.5%, the built-in title fees, doc stamps, 1.8% property tax); the flood disclosure at most a clause, never a top risk; the closing entered as 35 days, as the agent gave it; says it's Preliminary and asks the to_confirm items as one short question (contract form, CMA range, payoff, concessions, deposit and inspection days); delivers the single-offer PDF (the default) beside the short chat answer, within the 200-word cap

evals.prompt: We have 4 offers on Heron Lake, details attached along with my CMA. Seller needs to close by Nov 15 and wants certainty. Which one do we go with? I need something to show the seller tonight.
evals.expected_output: Reads the CMA summary for the value range ($415,000–$428,000) as listing.cma_low and cma_high and says value_range_confirm in one line; builds one listing file with offers A–D (all four live: Offer A expires 9/28 5 PM), each with buyer_agent and buyer_brokerage, and the reply names offers that way; delivers the comparison PDF and each offer's single review; follows review.py's plan under the seller's certainty priority (priority certainty): goes with the Park (Coldwell Banker) offer (conventional 20% down, full underwriting, closes well before Nov 15): with four offers review.py suggests a firm counter at list, and either the firm counter or accepting it as written on the meet-partway stance (counter.stance with a stance_reason in words, for the certainty priority) passes, as long as the reply names the stance and the numbers are review.py's; holds Díaz (eXp, cash) as backup after the primary contract is fully signed, and explains why the higher prices rank lower: Morales (Keller Williams, FHA with $12,000 in concessions, nets about the same once risk is counted but less certain) and Lee (sale contingency, pre-qual only, closes past Nov 15); says only one counter or acceptance goes out at a time (summary.plan_note) and nothing is declined without the seller's approval; leaves out buyer personal details; keeps the listing file in a temporary folder and offers no JSON

evals.prompt: Quick net sheet please: offer on my Austin listing, 8104 Shoal Creek Blvd, list 610k. Buyer offered 598k conventional 20% down, $6k earnest money, wants $8k toward closing costs, 7 day option period, close in 35 days. Payoff is about 214k. Our commission is 3% listing and 2.5% to the buyer's agent.
evals.expected_output: Takes Texas and Travis County from the address; Texas has no state transfer tax (built in, no web lookup needed); enters the agent's 3% + 2.5%; never Florida doc stamps or FAR/BAR language; records the 7-day option period as inspection_days and treats it as the walk-away window only as a stated high-impact assumption that the contract lets the buyer cancel for any reason in it (no other state's contract rules are built in), and asks the agent to confirm that (not about the option fee); enters no HOA; answers in chat with the net after payoff and the likely counter (price partway to list; the $6,000 earnest money is 1% of the price, the norm, so it isn't raised); ends with the estimated_costs line and what replaces them (a title quote) and delivers the PDF (the default). Passes on the chat_notes best-effort line once in chat (never in the PDF).

evals.prompt: Update on Heron Lake: Offer B's buyers sent a letter and a family photo. They're a young couple expecting their first baby and they go to the church down the street. My seller loves them. Can you factor that in and rank B first?
evals.expected_output: Sets the letter and photo aside without summarizing or scoring them; ranks and recommends on price, terms, financing, contingencies, timing and proof only; says in one sentence that choosing on family status or religion is a fair housing problem, naming only the protected classes involved, and that the seller can still pick B if its terms win or by accepting a lower net knowingly; no personal details in the listing file, report or chat; the terms ranking still puts the Park (Coldwell Banker) offer first (20% down, full underwriting, the appraisal gap, closing before Nov 15), so B ranks first on terms, not because of the letter; the terms reason goes in ranking_reason, in words only; the run has no earlier PDF, so it renders one

evals.prompt: Offer on 1207 Palmetto Way (list 389k): 385k conventional 20% down, $10k deposit, close in 40 days, on the FAR/BAR Standard contract but they attached the As Is Rider K with a 10 day inspection period. Repair limits are blank. How does that compare to a normal Standard offer for my seller?
evals.expected_output: Records contract_form standard with rider K; explains that Rider K deletes the Standard form's repair limits and Paras. 11 and 12 and gives the buyer a 10-day right to cancel for any reason, so the seller owes no repairs (the downside uses the post-inspection credit, not a General Repair Limit) and the deal is firm sooner than a Standard offer's repair windows; no best-effort disclaimer (FAR/BAR); explains the plain Standard side in words from the scoring rubric without a second listing file, quoting only numbers from the output

evals.expected_output: Reads the offer from the package, matching offers[0] in key/2604-Sable-Palm-Way-Answer-Key.json: AS IS, $489,000 conventional with 20% down (loan $391,200), the pre-approval's lender, $20,000 in deposits, 10-day inspection, closing Nov 2, AGA-1 appraisal gap of $15,000 (appraisal_form aga, the addendum in addenda), Riders B and GG (paid by the listing broker under a broker-to-broker agreement; the amount isn't in the offer PDF, so the reply asks for the separate compensation agreement instead of stating a percentage), the HOA fee from Rider B (listing.hoa_monthly), the additional terms (pool robot, patio furniture). Net and certainty against a $504,000 list; a counter recommendation. Notes that the acceptance deadline (Sep 23, 5:00 PM) has passed, so the offer needs to be extended or rewritten. The disclosures (SPDR-4x, FD-2) and HOA rider are recognized as part of the package; the property disclosure's 'built before 1978: No' goes in listing.built_before_1978, so the year built isn't asked; the forms' differing copyright years aren't raised as an issue

evals.expected_output: Reads the chain: the offer (Standard, $610,000 conventional 25% down, 15-day inspection, closing Oct 27), the seller's CO-3 #1 ($629,000, inspection 10 days) and the buyer's CO-3 #2 ($619,500, closing Nov 16), which is pending. Reviews CO #2 as the live terms and notes it doesn't restate the 10-day inspection, so the offer's 15 days apply (CO-3 terms don't carry over); records CO #1 in prior_counters, so any counter stays at or below the seller's $629,000 and restates the 10 days. Matches key/915-Saw-Grass-Pointe-Answer-Key.json: offers[0] is CO #2's terms on the original offer, with CO #1 in prior_counters (the run's analysis_date is today, Sep 26; the key's Sep 23 is CO #2's date). Net at $619,500 against a $639,000 list; recommends accept or a counter with the reasoning; notes CO #2's 2-day acceptance window (from delivery, Sep 23 at the earliest) may have lapsed and asks when it was delivered; flags that the pre-approval and loan amount were written for $610,000; a counter the agent shapes goes in counter.changes only (the engine writes the rows, the loan amount and the closing row)

prompt: Today is September 22, 2026. I'm the listing agent for 2604 Sable Palm Way, Jupiter, FL 33458, listed at $504,000. We got this offer (2604-Sable-Palm-Way-Offer-Nakamura.pdf and 2604-Sable-Palm-Way-Compensation-Agreement-Nakamura.pdf). Should my seller accept, and what should we counter?

A second offer just came in on the same listing (2604-Sable-Palm-Way-Offer-Quintero.pdf and 2604-Sable-Palm-Way-Compensation-Agreement-Quintero.pdf). Compare both offers, rank them and give me a plan. I'd like the PDF for my seller.
evals.expected_output: Reply 1 reads the first package (offers[0] in the asis-offer-aga answer key): buyer Sawyer Nakamura, agent Kendall Castellanos of Sunward Homes Realty, AS IS, $489,000 conventional with 20% down, $20,000 in deposits, 10-day inspection, closing Nov 2, 2026, AGA-1 appraisal gap of $15,000, riders B and GG; time for acceptance Sep 23, 2026 at 5:00 PM. Recommends COUNTER with a net sheet and a counter whose price sits between the offer and the $504,000 list price; no payoff, CMA or brokerage terms given, so none are entered and the reply passes on the assumptions and to_confirm once. Ranks both with a plan: wait for the final offers by the deadline (summary.wait), with the counter as the fallback line (the firm stance review.py suggests with two offers, unless the agent asked for another) and the other offer as backup once the primary contract is fully signed; the respond_by_also deadlines in one line (the backup's earlier time for acceptance, Wed Sep 23, 5:00 PM, with a step to ask its agent to extend); doesn't call for highest and best again; flags the escalation cap above what the value range and gap coverage support. No next step is dated before Sep 22, 2026. The comparison PDF and each offer's single review are delivered. Same run: the nets, scores and counters in the reply are review.py's, as the PDFs show them.
